overview: Makuria was a medieval Nubian kingdom centered at Old Dongola. The capital’s churches, palace and elite houses reveal a city where religious and political institutions shared a fortified core.

items.text: Excavations in Dongola’s citadel revealed substantial church buildings. A large apse found in 2021 may belong to a cathedral; that identification remains a research interpretation.
The newly exposed apse carried two rows of monumental painted figures. Monumental church painting formed part of the capital’s visual culture.
The citadel contained a palace and large houses associated with church and state elites, showing residential as well as ceremonial uses.

Treaties with Egypt supported travel and trade across the frontier. An older synthesis describes exchange that included enslaved people and grain; political accommodation did not mean Nubian annexation.

The University of Warsaw describes gradual decline in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries and investigates the later community’s transformation. Its research proposal does not prove a single collapse date or total disappearance.
